question: When the same two-layer EBM has distinct cold- and warm-regime climate-feedback coefficients, does a raw global state/forcing representation expose model-class mismatch while an explicitly regime-gated representation recovers the exact local dynamics without changing the least-squares solver?
hypothesis: A single no-intercept linear map on [surface temperature, deep temperature, forcing] cannot exactly represent both feedback regimes and therefore retains nonzero discovery and confirmation error. A regime-gated feature map with separate cold and warm copies of those same three inputs is full rank and recovers both local linear transitions to floating-point precision. Swapping the regime labels at confirmation destroys that advantage.

datasets.quality_control_policy: non-feedback physical parameters remain the literature-fixed positive reference values

datasets.time_domain: fixed 0.25-year local transitions with separate immutable discovery and confirmation sample domains
datasets.quality_control_policy: feedback coefficients, threshold, minimum regime margin, exact validation substeps, split domains, sample counts, seeds, and fitting policy are immutable; any transition approaching the threshold closer than the declared margin fails closed

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: all cold and warm confirmation next-state samples predicted by one global raw state/forcing linear map fit only on discovery samples
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: both regimes and all confirmation samples are required

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: all confirmation next-state samples predicted by the regime-gated feature map fit only on discovery samples
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: both regimes and all confirmation samples are required

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: raw-global confirmation relative error minus regime-gated confirmation relative error

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: combined cold/warm discovery samples fit by one raw state/forcing linear map
combined cold/warm discovery samples fit by the regime-gated map
discovery design rank for [surface temperature, deep temperature, forcing]
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: complete raw discovery design is required

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: discovery design rank for separate cold and warm copies of the same three raw features
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: complete gated discovery design is required

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: confirmation error of the fitted gated map when every cold/warm semantic label is intentionally swapped
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: all confirmation samples and the fitted gated map are required

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: minimum distance from the feedback threshold across every exact validation substep of every discovery and confirmation transition

negative_controls: raw-global and regime-gated candidates use the same numpy.linalg.lstsq solver, no intercept, no regularization, the same physical targets, and the same discovery/confirmation samples

accepted physical transitions remain at least 0.5 K from the feedback threshold at all 64 validation substeps, so the local regime feedback coefficient is unambiguous and exact fixed-regime propagation applies
the gated representation only duplicates the same state/forcing features into cold and warm blocks; it receives no exact transition matrix or target coefficients
confirmation samples never enter fitting or feature selection
swapped cold/warm labels preserve gated feature dimension while deliberately destroying regime semantics
falsifiers: any accepted physical transition approaches the feedback threshold inside the declared safety margin
the raw global map becomes effectively exact across both distinct feedback regimes
the correctly gated representation fails to recover confirmation transitions to floating-point tolerance despite full discovery design rank
swapped regime labels retain the correctly gated confirmation performance
the synthetic threshold or feedback coefficients are interpreted as an empirical real-climate tipping threshold or calibrated state dependence
split_policy: Fit both raw and gated maps only on fixture-pinned discovery samples from both regimes. Evaluate on separately seeded confirmation domains that are broader but remain safely inside their respective regimes.
preprocessing: No scaling or learned preprocessing. The raw feature vector is [surface temperature, deep temperature, forcing]. The gated representation concatenates cold-selected and warm-selected copies of that same raw vector.
stopping_rule: Report both model classes and the swapped-label negative control. The rung is internally consistent only if raw global mismatch remains visible, gated discovery/confirmation error is near floating-point precision, both design ranks are explicit, and every physical transition satisfies the regime margin.
multiple_comparison_policy: Both regimes, all domains, all four seeds, feedback coefficients, threshold, margin, feature maps, and solver policy are fixed by this experiment version.
